text:
matt: quick sync — weekly gpu runway readout. noticed us-west2 cluster A headroom is tighter than forecast, plus a small network throttling signal in AZ-b. can we triage?
leah: saw that on the dashboard this morning. us-west2-a cluster shows ~12.4k GPU hours remaining for the week vs forecasted 18k. burn rate spiked 22% after the nightly index jobs.
sara: index job spike is expected with the new retrain, but the preemptible mix jumped to ~35% this morning which cut effective throughput. throughput per-gpu is down ~7%.
juan: ops-bot posted an alert 10:03 — `net-throttle` on us-west2-az-b. packet drops ~0.6%, tail latency bump at the node level. link: <https://redwood.ops/dashboards/gpu-runway?region=us-west2|GPU Runway>.
ops-bot: automated alert: cluster=us-west2-a, az=az-b, metric=network_tx_drop, value=0.006, window=5m. Suggest checking host egress queues and top talkers.
matt: thanks. two things to decide: 1) short-term hedge for this week's burn; 2) remediation plan for the AZ throttling (could be infra or noisy tenant).
leah: short-term: shift 250 GPUs of batch-only capacity from us-east1 to us-west2 for 12 hours overnight. that buys ~8k GPU hours. downside: warmup time ~20m and infra quota checks.
sara: alternative is to throttle retrain batch jobs by 30% and bump inference routing to fallback `small-quant` models for non-critical paths. that reduces effectiveness but keeps latency SLOs.
juan: quota check: we have 400 available GPUs in us-east1 spare. Can we convert 250 to the right SKU? Some are Ampere and some are older; scheduler will pick matching flavor.
matt: prefer shifting GPUs if it remains faster than model fallback. leah, can you run the capacity-move script and estimate warmup window?
leah: running now. command: ```./infra/tools/capacity_move --from us-east1 --to us-west2 --count 250 --type a100```
leah: output: estimated warmup 17m, expected additional hourly capacity after warmup 250 GPUs * 1h = 250 GPU-hours/hr. will generate ~6k GPU-hours over 24h, but immediate relief is ~4.25k for remaining night window.
sara: combining with throttling retrain by 30% we net ~10k reduction in burn — should close the delta to forecast.
juan: on AZ throttling root cause: syslog snippet from node-12 shows repeated retransmits to a single internal ingestor IP, likely a noisy shard. snippet: ```May 3 10:01 host-12 kernel: tx_queue_full: dev eth0 dropped 120 packets to 10.11.22.33```
matt: action items: leah to start capacity move now, sara to roll throttle policy to retrain jobset (30%) via flag `--max-concurrency 0.7`, juan to open a ticket with networking to sweep AZ-b and contact noisy tenant owners. i'll update leadership on runway.
leah: started infra task at 10:06, ETA warmup 17m. tracking: #runbook-link <https://redwood.runbooks/az-hedge-us-west2|Runbook>. :thumbsup:
sara: will push throttle change with canary 5% then 100% in 2m. posting PR link: <https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/4782|PR 4782>.
juan: opened ticket NET-1129, assigned to netops. included packet captures and host logs.
matt: thanks all. followup check-in in 45m here. if warmup and throttle close the gap we keep plan; if not, we escalate to burst to dedicated for specific routes.
ops-bot: runbook note: projected runway after actions ~18.8k GPU hours for the week (est), risk level: medium.
